profile.name: Md Ether Deowan
profile.title: PhD Candidate in Field Robotics
profile.department: Department of Mechanical and Industrial Engineering
profile.tagline: Navigation, perception, and decision autonomy for underwater and field robotic systems.
bio: Md Ether Deowan is a PhD candidate in the Field Robotics Lab at the Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU), where he researches navigation and decision autonomy for underwater and field robotic systems.

He holds a BSc in Electrical and Electronics Engineering and an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master's in Marine and Maritime Intelligent Robotics, with study tracks at the University of Toulon and Jaume I University.
His work spans AI-driven perception, sensor fusion, robot control, multi-robot coordination, industrial automation, and human–robot collaboration.

researchThemes.title: Underwater robot autonomy
researchThemes.description: Robust navigation and decision-making for underwater vehicles operating with uncertain sensing and limited communication.

researchThemes.title: Multimodal perception and sensor fusion
researchThemes.description: Combining sonar, vision, Doppler, inertial, and other sensing modalities for localisation, mapping, and safe control.

researchThemes.title: Learning and model-based control
researchThemes.description: Reinforcement learning, predictive control, dynamic modelling, and hybrid autonomy for robotic systems.

researchProgram.title: Autonomous Decision-Making for UUVs in Dynamic Environments
researchProgram.summary: My PhD research explores how underwater robots can navigate and make reliable decisions in uncertain, dynamic environments, with emphasis on safe autonomy for inspection and exploration.
researchProgram.context: Underwater environments challenge robotic systems with changing visibility, uncertain sensing, currents, repetitive structures, and moving obstacles. My work investigates how perception, planning, and control can be connected to improve reliable autonomous operation.
